item.title: Tanabe: Castle Ruins and the Gateway to the Kumano Kodo — Guide
item.description: Tanabe, a port town on Wakayama’s western coast, is best known today as the main gateway to the Kumano Kodo, where most pilgrims begin their journey and where the excellent Kumano Tourism Bureau helps foreign walkers arrange routes and lodging. The town itself rewards a wander: the stone walls and water gate of Tanabe Castle survive near the harbour, Morihei Ueshiba, the founder of aikido, was born here and is remembered at a memorial hall, and after dark the narrow lanes of the Aji-koji district fill with small izakaya serving the day’s catch.
